about.aboutMeText1: As a developer with a keen eye for design and a love for coding, I specialize in building cutting-edge web applications that prioritize reactivity and user-friendliness. Leveraging the latest technologies and AI-assisted development workflows, my goal is to create an optimal user interface that strikes a delicate balance between aesthetics and functionality. I firmly believe that a truly exceptional UI architecture seamlessly integrates the objectives and requirements of the end-users, resulting in an elegant, efficient, and robust design that enhances the overall user experience.
about.aboutMeText2: Full-Stack Engineer with {{expYears}} years and {{expMonths}} months of experience in developing modern, reactive, and user-friendly web applications using the latest technologies. Specializing in creating a perfect blend of UI architecture that accounts for goals, needs, and design constraints. Proficient in React.js, Redux.js, JavaScript, TypeScript, Node.js, Tailwind CSS, and AI-assisted development. Experienced in building scalable web applications, Serverless computing with Azure, and responsive user interfaces.
about.techStackSubtitle: A look into how I choose the right tool for the job.
about.reactReduxUseCase: Complex, state-heavy enterprise applications requiring strict data flow.
about.reactReduxTradeoffs: Excellent ecosystem and debugging tools, but introduces boilerplate. For simpler apps or static content, I prefer Next.js or raw React Context API to avoid over-engineering.
about.nodeExpressUseCase: Fast, scalable microservices and APIs with high I/O operations.
about.nodeExpressTradeoffs: Great for real-time apps (WebSockets) due to the event loop. However, for heavily CPU-bound tasks (like image processing), I'd advocate for Go or delegating to serverless functions.
about.azureUseCase: Event-driven architecture and scaling specific endpoints without managing infrastructure.
about.azureTradeoffs: Highly cost-effective and infinitely scalable. The downside is potential cold starts and vendor lock-in. Mitigation strategies involve keeping functions warm and decoupling core logic.
about.tailwindUseCase: Rapid prototyping and maintaining design systems across large teams.
about.tailwindTradeoffs: Tailwind speeds up development and prevents dead CSS. However, for highly custom, math-heavy animations or complex component libraries (like this portfolio), I still leverage the power of SCSS (BEM).

studies.problem: I thought initially to build a basic application with mock data but then I thought of building a more complex and advanced application that uses user's location to fetch their nearby stores to show them restaurant they are familiar with, so I built this app with real time restaurant data.
